definitions.explanation: The price the seller names, before any haggling. Usually used when the buyer either accepts it without negotiating or complains that it is too high.

examples.english: I bought it at the asking price.

examples.japanese: {相手|あいて}の{言|い}い{値|ね}をそのまま{払|はら}うつもりはない。
examples.english: I have no intention of simply paying the other party's asking price.

examples.japanese: {市場|いちば}では{言|い}い{値|ね}から{交渉|こうしょう}が{始|はじ}まるので、そのまま{払|はら}う{人|ひと}はいない。
examples.english: At the market, negotiation starts from the asking price, so nobody pays it as it stands.

notes:
The stem of {言|い}う (to say) + {値|ね} (price): the price that is said. Do not confuse it with the いいね of social-media "likes", which is written in kana.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {言|い}い{値|ね}で{買|か}う: to buy at the asking price
- {言|い}い{値|ね}を{払|はら}う: to pay the asking price
- {言|い}い{値|ね}どおり: exactly as quoted

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {付|つ}け{値|ね}: bid price — the price the buyer offers, the counterpart of {言|い}い{値|ね}
- {定価|ていか}: list price — the fixed retail price, not open to negotiation
